candidate.title: SCMDA
candidate.scope: SCMDA (Single-Cell Multiple Displacement Amplification) as depicted in the middle row of the assigned Illumina poster crop, including the embedded SCcaller readout component. The upper MDA/IMS-MDA/MIDAS row and lower MALBAC row are adjacent context, not alternative targets of this SCMDA card. The single-cell-to-genome cartoon and gray panel describe the same per-cell architecture. The paper clarifies low-temperature lysis, the primer interpretation and the broad sequencing/variant-calling interface; the drawn S1 nuclease step is retained as diagram-level evidence without claiming it is part of the published SCMDA implementation.

method_scopes.rationale: All listed operations apply to the SCMDA row at declared schematic scope. The paper establishes SCMDA and SCcaller as a combined single-cell genome amplification and variant-analysis architecture; SCcaller is an embedded component rather than another target workflow. The two Synthesis captions denote successive local stages. S1 nuclease is retained only because it is explicitly drawn; its use in the primary implementation remains unverified. The broad library interface is paper-supported, not visibly expanded in the poster. The primary localizes the defining low-temperature change to lysis and DNA denaturation; the gray panel is not taken to establish on-ice phi29 synthesis. The generic library boundary is an explicit inference connecting the diagram endpoint, not an attribution of the paper’s particular kit to S1-treated DNA.

checks.rationale: Accept at the declared SCMDA schematic scope. Independent inspection confirms the target row, all material transformations, successive synthesis instances, the retained S1 route, DNA readout carrier, and SCcaller interface. Both multi-input operations are genuine joint interactions: template plus primers for annealing, and sequencing data plus hSNP information for calling. No independent biological branches are collapsed, no pooling is introduced, and all operation inputs/outputs agree with their flows. The primer correction is bounded by the primary evidence. The generic library interface is explicitly inferred; S1 use in the published implementation remains unestablished and is not asserted. No consequential unsupported claim or omitted in-scope branch remains.
